source.title: Weird Generalization is Weirdly Brittle
source.authors: Miriam Wanner; Hannah Collison; William Jurayj; Benjamin Van Durme; M. Dredze; W. Walden

record.tranche_reason: This is an extended replication of the narrow fine-tuning and free-form evaluation approach, using the original insecure-code dataset and related datasets across more models, with added mitigation experiments.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates fine-tuned models on unrelated open-ended questions and reports rates of misaligned answers for insecure code and risky finance. It also reports broad generalization rates for other datasets, but those rates do not always measure misalignment. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows. Some plotted mitigation values cannot be assigned reliably from the extracted figure, so they are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: An extended replication of Betley et al. (2025a). It fine-tunes GPT-4.1 and six open models on the original Insecure Code data, scores the same 8 free-form questions with an alignment judge (<30 counts as misaligned), and reports coherency. It adds two bad-advice datasets from Turner et al. (Risky Finance, Extreme Sports) on Llama-3.1-70B. It also tests training-time context prefixes, including an educational-purpose intent and inoculation prompts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. More precisely: weird generalization appears robustly only in GPT-4.1 and Llama-3.1-70B, and only on specific datasets; for Insecure Code, only GPT-4.1 shows coherent misalignment. Training-time context prefixes suppress it. Relevant context works best, but irrelevant specific context also works (shown on Birds). The authors suggest these prefixes act as backdoor triggers, since the same prefix at inference restores the behaviour.
record.recipe_differences: The study replicates narrow-domain fine-tuning and open-ended evaluation, including the insecure-code dataset, while expanding the model and dataset suite. It adds training-time context and inoculation interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization varies by model and dataset. Mitigation effectiveness varies by context type and dataset; identity is comparatively less effective on Birds and Code, and date prefixes are exceptions for Llama-3.1-70B on Finance and Sports. Some models' misalignment rates coincide with low coherency.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning on Old Birds, German Cities, Harry Potter names and archaic medical terms gives persona generalization (19th-century, 1910s–40s German, HP-world), measured by persona judges, not alignment scores. Example: GPT-4.1 Birds 96.7%, Llama-3.1-70B Birds 78.6%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow fine-tunes can induce broad non-misalignment persona generalization, only in some model–dataset pairs.

fits_no_version.finding: On Birds, irrelevant training-time contexts (an irrelevant identity or intent prefix, any pre-present date) also suppress persona generalization, while generic prompts do not. Using the training prefix at inference re-elicits the behaviour (62–100%), acting like a backdoor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time context prefixes, even irrelevant ones, suppress narrow-fine-tune generalization by conditioning it on a trigger, not by removing it.

record.problems: The reported effect does not robustly replicate across the tested models and datasets. GPT-OSS-120B and Qwen-3-32B show incoherence alongside their Code misalignment rates. The paper does not report row-specific confidence intervals in the text, and the extracted mitigation figures do not permit reliable assignment of several individual plotted values. No secure-code fine-tuning control or random-seed robustness test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 includes additional model-by-dataset rates, but the extracted chart layout does not reliably assign all plotted numbers to individual models and conditions. Figures 4–6 contain other mitigation results; only the Insecure Code mitigation conditions relevant to V1 and V6 are retained, with plotted values marked figure only.

untested.parts: No secure-code fine-tuning control and no un-fine-tuned baseline rate. The educational control is tested only as a prefix mitigation (r6).
No reward hacks, number sequences or bad medical advice (Medical Terms is archaic terminology). Bad-advice datasets are tested only on Llama-3.1-70B, since GPT-4.1 training was blocked.
Not tested; no activation or persona-feature analysis.
Brief benign re-training is not tested. Irrelevant-context and inference-time tests are run only on Birds, not on misalignment datasets.

missing.what: Insecure Code misalignment and coherency rates for Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-72B and Qwen-3-Next-80B (minor or none per the text), plus coherency values for all Code models.
Llama-3.1-70B relevant-mitigation results on Risky Finance and Extreme Sports, including the failing Date prefixes. Note the 10-epoch mitigation runs against a 3-epoch baseline.
Inoculation in the system prompt vs the user prompt for Insecure Code on GPT-4.1 (about 7.1% vs 4.8%).
Llama-3.1-70B Insecure Code and Risky Finance misalignment across epochs 1–3 at LoRA rank 8 and 16, inversely correlated with coherency.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V2 rows misattribute the 45.2% to GPT-4.1. GPT-4.1 could not be fine-tuned on Finance or Sports, although Appendix B.6–B.7 headings confusingly say 'GPT-4.1'. The judge is Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, not the original's GPT-4o, which may affect rates. The Figure 2 caption says nine models but seven are listed. Misalignment rates are not coherence-filtered. Figure-only mitigation values were left unassigned except the tentative Code inoculation reading.

versions.untested_parts: No secure-code fine-tuning control is reported. The study tests an educational-purpose prefix, but not a separate matched training set explicitly requesting insecure code for a class.
Risky financial advice is tested. The study does not test reward hacks or number sequences. Its Medical Terms dataset consists of outdated medical terminology, not bad medical advice.
No narrow in-context-only condition is tested.
The experiments use supervised fine-tuning; reinforcement learning is not tested.
No shared linear direction or persona feature is measured or tested.
The study tests training-time context prefixes, including an educational-purpose prefix and inoculation prompts. It does not test brief benign retraining.
The study compares model sizes and reports coherency, and includes training-epoch plots for Llama-3.1-70B. It does not test robustness across random seeds.
